drug_class: Mixed opioid receptor agonist-antagonist / IBS-D medication
purpose: Eluxadoline is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea, also called IBS-D, in adults. It helps reduce the belly pain and loose, frequent stools that come with this condition. It is meant for long-term use to help manage your symptoms day to day.
how_it_works: Eluxadoline works by acting on special receptors in your gut called opioid receptors. It helps slow down the movement of your intestines and reduces pain signals in your belly. Think of it as helping to calm down an overactive gut so things move more normally and you feel less discomfort.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, constipation, stomach pain, and vomiting. Some people also notice gas or a feeling of fullness. Constipation can sometimes be bothersome, so let your doctor know if it becomes a problem.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you do not have a gallbladder, drink more than a moderate amount of alcohol, or have certain liver or pancreas problems, as it can cause serious pancreatitis or a spasm of a bile duct. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have sudden, severe stomach pain. It is a controlled substance, so only take it exactly as prescribed.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken by mouth twice a day with food, once in the morning and once in the evening. If you cannot tolerate this dose or have certain health conditions, your doctor may lower it to 75 mg twice a day. Always take it with a meal.
